summary: This `app.jsx` file defines a foundational React functional component named `app`, exported as the default export. It imports React and currently renders a simple `<div>` wrapper with placeholder text ("asas"). As the primary entry point component of a React application, `app.jsx` serves as the root container where global layouts, state management providers, routing configurations, and child components are typically integrated to build the overall application UI.

This CSS stylesheet defines the layout and visual presentation for a web application page, likely displaying product or restaurant listings. Key features include:

- A global reset enforcing `box-sizing: border-box` and zero margins/padding.
- A flexbox-based header with a rounded search input, logo formatting, and navigation styling.
- Main content layout (`.res-container`) featuring item cards (`.cart`) with custom hover transitions, shadows, and image styling.
- A styled footer section.
- Skeleton UI loading states (`.shimmer-*`) utilizing dynamic `@keyframes` animations (`shimmermove`) to create smooth shimmer effects over placeholder elements while data loads asynchronously.

The `notes.html` file acts as the minimal entry point for a single-page web application. It sets up standard HTML5 metadata and responsive viewport settings, links to `notes.css` for styling, and provides an empty `<div id="root">` container. This container serves as the DOM mounting point where dynamic content is injected. Finally, it loads `notes.js` as an ES module, which executes the application logic and dynamically renders the UI into the root element.

This `notes.js` file is an archival scratchpad capturing the progressive learning of core React fundamentals. It contains commented-out code tracing the transition from low-level `React.createElement` calls to JSX syntax, functional component creation, and prop usage. Later snippets demonstrate building layout components (such as restaurant food-card displays), iterating over dynamic mock datasets using `Array.prototype.map()`, assigning unique `key` attributes, and integrating module imports. The file serves as a historical reference log for foundational React concepts including elements, components, props, layout structure, and dynamic list rendering.

This `package.json` configures a CommonJS JavaScript project utilizing React 19 for UI rendering and Axios for API requests. It defines a `dev` script that uses Parcel to bundle `notes.html`. Development dependencies include Parcel for bundling and ESLint for code quality. Additionally, it features an `allowScripts` block to grant build script execution permissions for specific native performance packages, including `@parcel/watcher`, `@swc/core`, `lmdb`, and `msgpackr-extract`.

The `Body` React component renders the main content area based on the `url` prop containing item data. If `url` is `null` (loading state), it renders a `shimmer-container` displaying 17 `Shimmer` placeholder components for a skeleton UI loading effect. When `url` contains data, it maps over the array within a `res-container` div, rendering a `Card` component for each element using `elem.info.id` as the unique key and passing data via the `resDetails` prop. Effectively, it acts as a layout container managing loading skeleton states and rendering item lists.

summary: The `FilterBtn` React component renders a button that filters a dataset of restaurants to display only top-rated entries. It accepts the dataset (`url`) and a state updater function (`setUrl`) as props. When clicked, the button filters the `url` array to retain only restaurant objects where `info.avgRating` is strictly greater than 4.2. It then invokes `setUrl` with the filtered array, updating the parent component's state to reflect only high-rated restaurants.

The component wraps a `div` element styled with the CSS class `footer` inside a container `div`. It serves as a visual layout component intended to be integrated into broader application pages or layout templates to ensure consistent page footers across the user interface.

summary: This React functional component, `Shimmer`, renders a skeleton loading placeholder UI for content cards. It creates structural layout placeholders using styled `div` elements with CSS classes (`shimmer-card`, `shimmer-hr`, `shimmer-img`, and `shimmer-name1` through `3`) to represent a divider, image, and text lines. The component improves user experience by serving as a visual loading state while underlying data is being asynchronously fetched.

The `components/cards.js` file defines and exports a default React functional component named `Card`. It accepts a `resDetails` prop containing restaurant metadata. The component renders a visual UI card consisting of an image—constructed by appending `resDetails.info.cloudinaryImageId` to `baseUrl`—and a details section displaying the restaurant's name (`resDetails.info.name`), cuisines (`resDetails.info.cuisines`), and average rating (`resDetails.info.avgRating`). It uses CSS classes `cart`, `cart-img`, and `cart-details` for layout and styling.

The `components/url.js` file acts as a centralized configuration module storing essential API and CDN endpoints for the application. It exports `swiggyUrl`, a CORS proxy-wrapped endpoint configured with specific latitude/longitude coordinates to fetch Swiggy restaurant listings. It also exports `baseUrl`, the root path for Swiggy’s Cloudinary CDN, pre-configured with image transformation parameters (lossy compression, auto-format, and 660px width) for rendering restaurant images. Centralizing these URLs ensures code reusability, easier maintenance, and consistent data fetching across the app.
